To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the accuracy of dose calculations in the treatment of breast cancer depends on the photon energy, the lateral depth of dose reference point below skin surface, and the treatment planning system algorithm used.

the accuracy of dose calculation for tangentially-irradiated breast cancer patients is improved by a factor of 2-3 when changing from a two-dimensional (2-D), to a three-dimensional (3-D), treatment planning system (TPS) algorithm.
the 3-D algorithm gives more accurate dose calculations for breast tangential photon fields than the 2-D algorithm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of two- and 3-dimensional (2-D/3-D) photon dose calculations for tangential breast irradiation.
the accuracy of two- and 3-dimensional photon dose calculation algorithms for tangential breast irradiation.
the accuracy of two-dimensional and three-dimensional photon dosimetry for tangential irradiations of the breast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3-D algorithm is superior to the 2-D algorithm.
3-D photon dose calculations should be performed for all breast tangential fields.
3-D photon dose calculations are more accurate than 2-D dose calculations for tangential irradiations of the intact breast.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
3-D algorithms are more accurate than 2-D algorithms in dose calculation.

for the 3-D TPS, the agreement between measured and calculated dose was within +/-5% for all lateral isocenter depths and photon energies, while for the 2-D TPS, agreement with measurement varied from +/-3 to +/-10% depending on the photon energy and lateral depth of the reference point below the surface.
the 3-D algorithm is a more reliable method of dose calculation for tangentially-irradiated breast.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for the breast, the use of 2-D dose calculation algorithms can lead to significant errors.

for tangential irradiations of the breast, 3-D dose calculation is necessary for accurate dose calculation, especially at the lateral surface of the breast, where the dose can be overestimated by as much as 10% when a 2-D calculation algorithm is used.
the use of a 3-D TPS for breast irradiation is essential to ensure accurate dose calculations.
